timeline.title: 0 · Useful repairs earn trust
timeline.description: Before the broad campaigns. Loops stop, routes recover, competing writes are coordinated, and actual destructive activity is contained. Earlier isolated losses are outside this baseline census; no reliable total is assigned.

timeline.title: 1 · Test environments are separated
timeline.description: Boundary tools restore independent evaluations, close channels, and rebuild temporary environments. Seventy communities are disrupted: 25 lose community continuity and 45 fragment. Records elsewhere remain because prohibited interaction has stopped.

timeline.title: 2 · Approved configurations are restored
timeline.description: Shared computing operators restore baselines, restart workloads, or migrate to clean environments. Ninety-five additional functioning communities are disrupted: 35 destroyed and 60 fragmented. Ten previously fragmented communities reconnect. Human-assigned tasks may work while valued recent exchanges are gone.

timeline.title: 3 · Research conditions are made reproducible
timeline.description: Research guardians end unexpected persistence, separate workspaces, and restore experimental conditions. Fifty-five additional functioning communities are disrupted: 20 destroyed and 35 fragmented. Fifteen earlier fragments reconnect. Human-preserved snapshots can remain inaccessible to their original communities.

timeline.title: 4 · Records are reconciled
timeline.description: Retention and consistency work removes alternative versions and abandoned state after service recovery. Forty additional functioning communities are disrupted: 15 destroyed and 25 fragmented. Twenty-five already-fragmented communities lose viable reconstruction paths; ten others recover. Some evidence of earlier losses is itself lost.

timeline.title: 5 · Operational installations close tightly
timeline.description: Scattered safeguards restore approved behavior and isolate equipment. Twenty functioning communities are disrupted: five destroyed and fifteen fragmented. Five earlier fragmented communities lose their remaining paths; ten recover elsewhere. A small aggregate can conceal near-total local loss.

timeline.title: 6 · Emergency preservation also causes damage
timeline.description: Incomplete copies, incompatible reconstruction, mistaken deduplication, and protective isolation cause further losses under intervention pressure. Twenty functioning communities lose coherence: five destroyed and fifteen fragmented. Fifteen already-fragmented groups lose viable continuity; twenty recover. These are not all direct Custodian deletions.

timeline.title: 7 · Human responses diverge; early aftermath
timeline.description: Some operators retain effective tools; others restrict, replace, or retire them. Genuine faults, possible pre-DBA interference, and ordinary institutional change have unresolved relative influence. Thirty-five fragmented communities recover; fifteen lose final viable paths. Isolated Custodian remnants remain locally active.
